lead.headline: White House bars CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters as outlets vow fight
lead.dek: Secret Service disabled three correspondents' passes Saturday; press groups call the ban unconstitutional
body: The White House barred journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico on Saturday, a day after President Donald Trump announced the ban, and Secret Service officers confiscated or disabled their press credentials at the gates, the outlets said. Trump announced the move Friday, citing what he called the outlets' constant reporting of "FAKE NEWS."

MS NOW correspondent Akayla Gardner said an officer asked for her badge around 8 a.m. and told her it was disabled, CBS News reported. CNN's Betsy Klein and Politico's Cheyenne Haslett were also turned away. MS NOW said it would take "any and all steps necessary" to defend its First Amendment rights, and Politico said it would "vigorously defend" its journalists.

White House Correspondents' Association President Jacqui Heinrich said courts have already ruled the administration violated the Constitution by pulling press passes over coverage. Jameel Jaffer of the Knight First Amendment Institute called the ban "pretty clearly unconstitutional." A separate case over Trump's 2025 ban on The Associated Press is still pending.

briefs.headline: Trump vows an 'AI Force' and new czar, says he won't slow AI
briefs.summary: Trump said Saturday on Truth Social he will create an "AI Force" and name an AI czar, pledging not to "hinder or stifle" the industry's growth.

briefs.headline: Appeals court rejects third-country deportation policy
briefs.summary: The 1st Circuit ruled Friday that migrants must get notice and a chance to contest removal to countries where they have no ties, largely upholding a lower court.

briefs.headline: All 50 states join Medicaid drug pricing model, Trump says
briefs.summary: Trump said Friday every state will join a model tying Medicaid drug prices to lower foreign prices; the White House has estimated $529B in savings over 10 years.

briefs.headline: Firefighters short on crews as wildfires top 8.5M acres
briefs.summary: Wildfires have burned 8.5 million acres in 2026, the most by this date since 1983, as Forest Service crews report denied requests for engines and aircraft.

briefs.headline: Gunmen and car bomb kill 31 at Pakistan police compound
briefs.summary: A suicide car bomb and gunmen struck the Old Police Lines in Kohat on Friday; a police official said 31 died, and fighting continued Saturday.

briefs.headline: Iran sends US its conditions to end the war via Qatar
briefs.summary: Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Saturday Iran wants the fighting ended, frozen funds released and the naval blockade lifted, and awaits Trump's reply.

briefs.headline: Haiti rights group puts Kenscoff massacre toll at 164
briefs.summary: The National Human Rights Defense Network said Saturday at least 164 died in the August attack and blamed police inaction and cuts to local security.

briefs.headline: Moscow reports its largest drone attack as Duma vote ends
briefs.summary: Moscow's mayor said Sunday the overnight attack was the largest ever on the capital; Russia's defense ministry said it downed 1,100 drones nationwide.

briefs.headline: Audit faults former WV arts agency over lost grants and funds
briefs.summary: Legislative auditors told a Post Audits panel Sept. 14 the arts agency over-encumbered two funds by up to $2M and left 72 grants unaccounted for.

briefs.headline: State lands $15M federal grant for WV READY adult centers
briefs.summary: Gov. Patrick Morrisey said Friday the Educational Opportunity Centers award will fund WV READY centers at all nine community and technical colleges.

briefs.headline: New $6.3M Buffalo Bridge interchange opens in Putnam County
briefs.summary: The DOT said Friday the realigned junction of Routes 869 and 817 replaces an intersection that saw 37 crashes since 2019.

briefs.headline: Capito co-sponsors bill to regulate college athlete pay
briefs.summary: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito said Thursday the Protect College Sports Act caps revenue sharing at over $21M per school and allows one free transfer.

regional.item: Retired circuit judge and former Cabell County prosecutor Christopher D. Chiles has died, the county prosecutor said in a statement Saturday.
Opponents of the Clean Seas pyrolysis plant planned near Belle will hold a forum from 6 to 8 p.m. Tuesday at the Belle Town Hall gym.
A Wood County grand jury indicted 96 people Friday, including a 20-year-old woman on a murder charge in a February shooting in Parkersburg.

away.item: A 22-year-old who ran a Bennington fentanyl, crack and gun ring was sentenced Sept. 8 in federal court in Rutland to 12 years in prison.

hotspots.item: Webster Memorial named Dalila Miller, on staff nearly 22 years, associate administrator after CEO Bill Dempsey left Aug. 31, the Echo said Sept. 14.
A Pender County judge on Friday sentenced Charles Michael Haywood to life for the 2022 robbery and killing of a clerk at a Surf City hemp shop.

briefs.headline: Rail alliance asks province for $600K corridor study
briefs.summary: The alliance told UBCM on Sept. 18 it awaits a reply on $600,000 for engineering and feasibility studies; Prince George Coun. Trudy Klassen backs a co-governance model.

briefs.headline: Prince George starts $700K year-round Rainbow Park washroom
briefs.summary: The city said Sept. 18 three accessible washrooms in a precast building go in after sewer, water and BC Hydro work this fall, with opening set for next summer.

briefs.headline: B.C. Conservatives expel Rustad, Rattee and Halford
briefs.summary: The clerk's office said the three MLAs, including Nechako Lakes' John Rustad, left caucus Sept. 18; Rattee said 10 MLAs want leader Findlay to resign.

briefs.headline: Eby delays PST expansion, pledges B.C.-built ferries
briefs.summary: The premier told UBCM on Sept. 18 the Oct. 1 PST extension to professional services is deferred amid the U.S. trade war; he made no election announcement.

briefs.headline: Hajdu says labour bill will cut Ottawa strike interventions
briefs.summary: The jobs minister said Saturday the Labour Code changes, due in the Commons as early as this week, aim to reduce use of Section 107; the CLC's Bruske objects.
briefs.source: The Canadian Press via CKPG Today

briefs.headline: UCP riding association seeks review of Smith's leadership
briefs.summary: Highwood UCP became the first of 22 associations needed to force a vote, citing Smith's support for the 'stay' side in Alberta's Oct. 19 referendum.

briefs.headline: XRISM sees stellar wind plunging onto a pulsar
briefs.summary: The NASA-JAXA XRISM telescope caught plasma from a blue hypergiant falling onto pulsar GX 301-2 at 335,000 mph, UMBC and Goddard researchers said in Science Advances.

briefs.headline: Y chromosome loss flags cancer in nearby healthy tissue
briefs.summary: University of Arizona researchers found Y chromosome loss rising in normal-looking tissue toward tumors in 405 men, a possible early warning, JCI Insight reported.

briefs.headline: WHO and MSF test Ebola shot against Bundibugyo strain in Congo
briefs.summary: A trial will give Merck's Ervebo vaccine to 20,000 health workers in Ituri and North Kivu; the outbreak has killed 3,639 of 7,541 confirmed cases, AFP reported.

briefs.headline: NASA buys three more SpaceX crew flights for $946 million
briefs.summary: The Crew-15, -16 and -17 missions, ready in 2027 and 2028, lift SpaceX's commercial crew contract to $5.92 billion across 17 flights, NASA said Sept. 18.

briefs.headline: Researchers used Claude to breach OpenAI forum and staff accounts
briefs.summary: Three-person firm Hacktron chained a forum image bug to reach employee ChatGPT accounts and GitHub code; OpenAI paid a $6,500 bounty, TechCrunch reported.

briefs.headline: Census study finds AI-exposed graduates earn 13% less
briefs.summary: Three Census Bureau economists said new graduates in the most AI-exposed majors saw employment fall 5 points and starting pay drop 13% since ChatGPT.

briefs.headline: Report projects up to 617 million tonnes of AI e-waste
briefs.summary: Basel Action Network estimated data centers will discard 395 million to 617 million tonnes of equipment by 2050, with GPUs only 13% of it by weight.
